rankings.strongest_idea: Introduce one parent-facing orchestration façade that directly reuses existing domain reducers, storage primitives, StateManager authority, and compatibility helpers while using Fugue only for shipped static-DAG and replay capabilities.

rankings.fatal_flaw: Its 12–16 week proliferation of brands, proof types, effect receipts, capability infrastructure, and phase-specific modules substantially exceeds the brownfield migration needed and raises long-term evolution cost despite matching Loom's type conventions.
rankings.strongest_idea: Use parser-produced CompleteRoster proofs so partial result sets cannot reach aggregation or tally states.

rankings.fatal_flaw: Requiring every operation, including status, to traverse dedicated Fugue DAGs plus hash-linked events, publication receipts, descriptor-anchored stores, and index compare-and-swap over-fortifies the existing architecture at 12–16 weeks of effort and creates more machinery than the codebase needs to own.
rankings.strongest_idea: Bind each semantic spawn to an immutable engine-issued grant and publication receipt so no request becomes executable before its complete artifact batch is durably accepted.
